messages:
Alex: Quick sync — we need to finalize the Rerank API contract for v1. Decision items: score type returned (raw logits vs normalized), top_k semantics when client asks > available candidates, and truncation policy for long candidate texts. Can folks chime in?
Maya: For perf, raw logits are cheapest to produce. Normalization (softmax) is O(n) per request but fine for small n. My ask: default to returning raw scores + a normalized_score when client requests it.
Sam: Agree with Maya. Also we should be explicit about numeric range and dtype (float32). Some clients expect [0,1].
Jesse: If we return both, we'll need to be careful with payload size. For large candidate lists (1000+), normalized scores double data sent. Maybe cap included normalized scores to top_k only.
Alex: Good point. Proposal: always return raw_score for every candidate, and only include normalized_score for the final returned top_k slice. If client sets include_normalized=true, we compute softmax just for those returned items.
Liam: How about tie-breaking/sort stability? Customers want stable order across reruns for same scores. That complicates internal shuffling/batching. I propose stable sort by (score desc, original_index asc) unless client asks for randomized tie-break.
Eva: +1 on stable sort default. Add param tie_break: ["stable","random"] with default stable. Document non-determinism when random chosen.
Maya: Truncation policy: we have two concerns — input payload tokenization for scoring and response payload size. For scoring we should allow passing full text but enforce a model-length cut (e.g., 4096 tokens) and document that we truncate candidate texts to model limit on the right. For response size, offer max_returned_candidates and a top_k param.
Sam: We also have to decide behavior when client asks top_k > candidate_count. Options: return only available candidates (no padding) or pad with nulls. I vote return only available candidates and set returned_count field.
Alex: Proposal summary: 1) params: top_k (int, default 10), max_candidates (server-side cap), include_normalized (bool), tie_break (stable|random), include_raw_scores (bool, default true). 2) Behavior: if top_k > n_candidates -> return n_candidates and set returned_count. 3) normalized_score only computed for returned top_k if requested. 4) stable sort by default.
Jesse: Launch gates? We need perf SLOs (p99 latency <= X ms for common top_k=10), evallist to detect score regressions, and a migration guide for customers using current rerank.v0.
Liam: Dev note: batching gains drop if we compute softmax across huge candidate sets per-request. Doing softmax on just the returned top_k keeps batching efficient.
Eva: SDKs: we should add helper that maps client-side embedding-based prefilter + rerank call. Doc example: ```json
{"query":"q...","candidates":[{"id":"a","text":"..."}],"top_k":5,"include_normalized":true}```
Maya: Security/compliance: no user PII should be sent in logs. Add redact policy to examples and opt-in request logging.
Alex: Ok next: who owns the API doc, the migration guide, and the perf tests? Maya + Sam for implementation; Jesse for rollout plan and migration doc; Eva for SDK updates and examples. I'll open a PR with the spec and a small strawman JSON schema tonight. Any objections?
Sam: No objections. I'll start a benchmark run with a 1k candidate workload to measure softmax cost and memory.
Jesse: I'll draft the rollout checklist: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%, with automatic fallback to v0 if error rate > 1% or latency spike > 2x baseline.
Alex: Great. One last thing: add a small field in response: scoring_metadata {"model_version":..., "score_type":"logit"} — string fields only in docs. Keep it small.
Maya: +1. Also callout that score calibration (to probabilities) is separate work (post-v1) — keep out of scope for initial launch.
Eva: I'll update SDK examples and add a migration FAQ item about top_k differences and stable sorting.
Alex: Thanks team. I'll drop the PR link here when ready. :pray:
